name: David Hogg
subject: This movement is working, Peter
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Older leaders are passing the torch — and we need bold young leaders to carry it forward.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260131-1&t=1&akid=3100%2E587540%2E02PUiP)
Peter,
Something real and powerful is happening right now.
Nancy Pelosi retired after 38 years in Congress. Steny Hoyer, the longest-serving House Democrat, is stepping down. All across the country, older leaders are recognizing the need for the new generation to take their turn. We’re grateful for their decades of service and are grateful that they are passing the torch to the next generation of game-changing leaders.
This is what we’ve been demanding for years. This is what an intergenerational movement looks like in action.
While we’re ready to see younger faces in office, here’s what I know: _Leaders We Deserve wouldn’t exist without older Americans who are fed up with the status quo and ready for something better._
**[Will you join them in contributing $5 to help us move forward?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260131_1_age.eh95d3&refcode=em20260131-3100&amount=5&t=2&akid=3100%2E587540%2E02PUiP)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260131_1_age.eh95d3&amount=5&refcode=em20260131-3100&t=21&akid=3100%2E587540%2E02PUiP)**
Some of our strongest grassroots supporters are decades older than the candidates we’re endorsing. But they remember being young, feeling unrepresented while fighting for reproductive justice, Civil Rights, democracy — before many of us were even born.
These are the same battles we’re in now, and our supporters are showing up and making damn sure this generation has a real shot.
**This movement is not about young vs. old.** It’s about progress. It’s about fighters vs. folders. Electing leaders who will stand up to current injustices and not give up the moment their donors become uncomfortable.
As the older generation steps aside, we only have a narrow window to elect young, bold leaders to fill these seats — and we can’t afford to waste it. We're supporting candidates like Zohran Mamdani, who is already delivering on his campaign promises just a few weeks into his term. We’re hitting college campuses to recruit young progressives. We’re doing the long-term work.
To do this work, we rely on the individual contributions of supporters like you — people of _all_ ages ready for a new wave of politics.
**[Will you contribute $5 to help us meet our end-of-month goals and keep building this movement?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260131_1_age.eh95d3&refcode=em20260131-3100&amount=5&t=22&akid=3100%2E587540%2E02PUiP)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260131_1_age.eh95d3&amount=5&refcode=em20260131-3100&t=23&akid=3100%2E587540%2E02PUiP)**
When a third of the country is Gen Z or Millennial but we barely have a fraction of the power, we’re failing to provide proper representation. That changes when we build a coalition across generations.
Thank you for your support.
— David Hogg

Peter Willis,

rapidly scaling up our work to take on the oligarchs. And we’re firing up
our powerful GOTV machine for primaries that are just weeks away to get
the bold leaders we need in office to make lasting change.

back. So we have an urgent goal of $9,654 to power our grassroots

| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8f5e1c76-58ce-4110-aff3-b751624e85a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar, the first held in the Arab world, was a glittering spectacle of soccer under the desert sun--but beneath the glamour lurked a storm of controversies over LGBTQ+ rights. Qatar's legal framework, rooted in Sharia law, criminalizes same-sex relations with up to seven years in prison (and theoretically harsher penalties like stoning, though rarely enforced), while public displays of affection by anyone are taboo. Homosexuality is viewed as "damage in the mind" by some Qatari officials, and campaigning for LGBTQ+ rights is also illegal.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.exaNHaLibQoLhvgBcSBg1X1uVgZ6vsr9f9Z50BUa5aw?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=186411746)
Four years and 7400 miles away in the rain-soaked emerald city of Seattle, where coffee flows like ideology and activism is as routine as ferry rides, the 2026 FIFA World Cup was supposed to be a triumphant global hug. But when organizers branded a knockout-stage match between Egypt and Iran as the official "[Pride Match](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/927fbe44-864b-4864-9fd0-07bd428b0009?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" at Lumen Field, they unwittingly lit a fuse under Mayor Katie Wilson's fledgling administration. Elected in November 2025 as Seattle's second self-described socialist mayor--riding a wave of frustration over housing costs and inequality--Wilson, a 43-year-old transit advocate and political newcomer, now stares down a perfect storm of clashing worldviews.

This isn't just soccer (futbol); it's a leftist cultural nightmare where rainbow flags, keffiyehs, and black bloc banners threaten to tangle into a diplomatic and domestic debacle.

At its core, the Pride Match embodies Seattle's progressive soul. The city's World Cup bid, led by the Seattle 2026 Host Committee, aimed to weave in local values like inclusivity and equity. Designating the Egypt-Iran game--slated for June 2026--as the [Pride Match](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/7434dd37-c6a4-488b-9885-4aea12137876?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was a nod to LGBTQ+ visibility, complete with planned pre-game events featuring drag performances, queer youth panels, and a sea of rainbow banners draping the stadium.

For Wilson, a [democratic socialist](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/2e92bf04-862e-4312-a64d-e03044a26f02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who campaigned on taxing the rich to fund social services and amplifying marginalized voices, this aligns perfectly with her platform. Her victory over incumbent Bruce Harrell, by a razor-thin margin in a city that's seen its share of leftist icons like Kshama Sawant, was fueled by promises of bold, unapologetic progressivism.

Hosting a Pride-infused spectacle? It's catnip for her base: the baristas unionizing in Capitol Hill, the tenant organizers in the Central District, and the queer activists who've long made Seattle a beacon for the rainbow diaspora.

Enter the collision course. Egypt and Iran, both with draconian laws criminalizing homosexuality--punishable by imprisonment or worse--have erupted in outrage.
Egypt's football federation fired off a letter to FIFA rejecting "any activities related to the so-called Pride Match," calling it an affront to their "cultural and religious values."

Iran's federation followed suit, lodging a formal objection and demanding relocation, citing the event's incompatibility with Islamic principles that view LGBTQ+ expression as haram.

While FIFA has so far shrugged off the complaints, insisting the match stays in Seattle, the diplomatic ripples are already lapping at Wilson's doorstep. As mayor, she's tasked with city coordination, from security to public events, thrusting her into a quagmire where her socialist solidarity with global oppressed groups clashes head-on with the realpolitik of hosting nations whose theocracies and autocracies brook no compromise on social issues.

The nightmare intensifies on the streets, where Seattle's eclectic fanbase promises chaos. Picture this: 68,000 souls packing Lumen Field, a microcosm of the city's progressive patchwork. On one side, throngs of LGBTQ+ soccer enthusiasts waving Pride flags, chanting for trans rights and marriage equality, their outfits a riot of glitter and green face paint for the USMNT-adjacent spirit. Seattle's queer community, bolstered by events like PrideFest and the ongoing fight against anti-trans legislation, sees the match as a victory lap for visibility. But rubbing elbows--or worse--with supporters from Egypt and Iran? Many of whom arrive with deep ties to conservative Muslim diasporas in the Pacific Northwest, waving national flags and perhaps even salafi banners. These fans, often devout and culturally conservative, view the Pride branding as Western decadence imposed on their sacred game. Tensions simmer: a rainbow scarf brushed against a hijab, a "Love is Love" sign eyed warily by a group chanting in Arabic. Whispers of boycotts from Egyptian-American communities in Bellevue could turn to vocal protests, forcing Wilson to navigate accusations of cultural imperialism from the very internationalist left she champions.

Then there's Antifa--the black-clad specter of Seattle's radical underbelly, ever-ready to "punch Nazis" but equally vigilant against perceived Islamophobia or state-sponsored homophobia. Antifa-aligned fans, notorious from the 2020 CHOP zone and ongoing clashes with far-right groups, might flood match-day tailgates with red-and-black flags, decrying Egypt's military-backed regime and Iran's Revolutionary Guard as fascist foils. Their rhetoric? "No Pride in Genocide" chants targeting both nations' records on Palestine and queer rights. Wilson, whose socialist cred includes endorsements from DSA chapters that overlap with Antifa networks, risks alienating her hard-left flank if she downplays the event's provocations. Yet cracking down on autonomous actions--say, a spontaneous die-in outside the stadium--would brand her a sellout to corporate FIFA interests, echoing the criticisms that sank Harrell's tenure. Imagine the optics: riot-geared SPD officers, whom Wilson pledged to defund, shielding Pride floats from black bloc fireworks while Iranian diplomats fume from VIP suites.

[Protest erupts at FIFA tournament amid U.S.-Iran tensions and Israeli-Gaza war.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/84ac5395-463e-40fc-8fb4-b6202b95b228?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
For Wilson, this isn't abstract ideology; it's a governance gut-punch. Her administration, barely a month old by December 2025, is already stretched thin by a homelessness crisis and tech-fueled gentrification.

The Pride Match amplifies every fault line: How does a socialist mayor square hosting a $1 billion World Cup spectacle amid austerity calls? Diplomatically, she must soothe FIFA's suits while fielding calls from the State Department about not embarrassing allies like Egypt, a key US partner in counterterrorism. Domestically, LGBTQ+ groups demand full-throated support, but Muslim advocacy orgs like the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) warn of rising hate crimes against their communities if the event veers into Islamophobic territory.

Antifa's volatility could spill into property damage, handing ammo to conservative critics nationwide who paint Seattle as a "commie hellhole".

"In this leftist labyrinth, Wilson's nightmare is the paradox of progressivism: championing universal human rights while respecting cultural sovereignty. Push too hard on Pride, and she alienates conservative Muslim voters and risks boycotts that tank the event's $200 million economic boost. Dial it back, and her base erupts, accusing her of betraying queer lives for soccer dollars. It's a microcosm of global left tensions--intersectionality fracturing under nationalism's weight. As one Outsports analyst quipped, "Egypt vs. Iran in Seattle's Pride Match? That's not a game; it's a geopolitical therapy session."

Ultimately, Wilson might thread the needle with hybrid events: a "Global Solidarity Festival" outside the stadium, blending queer storytelling with interfaith dialogues on justice. But the collision looms--Islam's conservative currents, LGBTQ+ exuberance, and Antifa's revolutionary fire--as a stark reminder that Seattle's socialist dreams crash against the world's jagged realities. It's clear: for Wilson, the Pride Match isn't just soccer. It's the beautiful game's brutal mirror, reflecting a left adrift in its own contradictions.

Register or check your status here: Your vote in the Republican Primary is critical to keeping Texas values strong in Washington. We need proven conservative fighters who will defend our freedoms, secure the border, support our law enforcement, and back President Trump's America First agenda. body:
Look – we have a lot of things moving in our favor right now. I outlined five here, but the list goes on.
[](https://links.trueamericanconservatives.com/s/c/B6Dk5zvNT9onJ-ZcxPRgXTDjtAG35xI_LgQ9Flyzbd4DmCGJ0MV6YveIzqM0W7TCNVbDqINeS6AyeXNVW_c-5Pg24rq5laPRwlDVxxnbN5EgyFPsoKvmGQ1gvGFMOGK5cx5-MuQxjh3DHiKTGV82CDbizSCQWH_x0ACLNa3l1EI4eWH8Cqb2ID8RexpqoyaI0NlNRWX3ezhX1vYr3Ycs_uIvmKgX2si-xWehP-SPCUF8_PttdGBrHfdHZKptXhRBPBepJc3SNLbEbHBhrz7ib-fHxO_OK8s2O-O5EXB6mnx6r8h5kSmLPK0JfDDqBYowKB-9AunhpQA_43OKPjMDLMI2Itr19W_0wwteeUXxB_QM_PSMuWLB1FZUNHIm4MhMXL0IO3N6O-qC0xpfIcl_2n2Jfg3iQb0H6XaiUfqLxy7aOKAvwzBmGcCzlfWsLd4FzRyNmtArAfiSBi-HI5qVdVjrQiZFxKwdVR6sy0Qww5opig3kOuMdwJV3kqzENXQyzjDRje2Fl2_hS-mY2OUL1YkhFBq_v1SRp-JCzmgaVJWC4mah07lA0fHkwR2LHkJo4JzoRsjt7x6ukQ3SLrQd9b61F4oc8lJXWOyTgNnxLLZ2yxzVj8Q1-PyvgruqhJX925KhrGUoQP9IivGn9MotSwdXLTFGzVEVgcxc3r53orgSpchiA3k6kNstbFzULIRinUoyCKpwfi7OqJXdCG_vEpej0pmSMJszC3m6ZZWAUwCkJXGGC2Xf/Rso1lfej1xGGt11vH4DqHqDjlTMDxl4f/17)Hi Peter - it's Michele!
We're about a week out since launching my campaign for U.S. Senate, so I thought I'd take a moment to explain how this race will be the biggest upset election in the country.
Here are the five reasons we're going to win:
REASON #1: Tim Walz and his inner circle have made our state into a laughingstock. The American people saw it live when a video exposing fraud in Minnesota went viral with 140,000,000 views. The far-Left is vulnerable, and they know it.
REASON #2: My main opponent was Walz's running mate and his right-hand. Peggy Flanagan is as extreme as they come and suffers from as much baggage as our corrupt Governor. The more voters hear, the more they'll reject her.
REASON #3: The far-Left is on the rise, and voters are noticing. I'm sure you saw when activists stormed a St. Paul church to intimidate Christians, attacked police officers, and potentially sent billions of dollars to fraudulent day cares.
REASON #4: I'm a political outsider. I don't owe anyone anything in politics, and special interests don't control me. I have a hunch voters want more folks in office who tell the truth, speak plainly, and have a spine. That's me to a T.
REASON #5: Our campaign is already surging. We have donors in all 50 states and just about every county in Minnesota. We have a winning message and a winning campaign; all we need is the resources to win.

| | Charlie would have wanted you to have this.

Before his September 10th assassination, Charlie had just put the finishing touches on a very important book. His final book.

The topic is one that Charlie found to be crucial for every human to understand and practice.

This isn't a book about public policy or political discourse, nor is it simply about passing on values of patriotism to young Americans.

**Instead, this book is about something far deeper and more personal -- the importance of honoring the Sabbath and resting in God's grace. **

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children.

By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: _**" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." **_

His book, _**Stop, in the Name of God**_ is the fruit of that conviction.

Charlie's hope was for each of us to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive...

A sacred routine meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and renew our strength for the battles to which He calls us.

I believe you will find this book inspiring.

Charlie wanted everyone to have this book because its message meant so much in his own life.

In the months since Charlie's assassination, there has been a massive surge of interest in Turning Point USA's message among young Americans...

...and it's not just the conservative message as a whole -- _**it 's the message of FAITH! **_

In recent months, I have heard countless stories of people who have answered Charlie's call to attend a Bible study, start a family, and pray to God.

Charlie devoted so much of his time urging people to build strong families, to go to church, and to stand up for America. _And it 's happening. _

After years of witnessing declining church attendance, we are now seeing Americans filling the pews in huge numbers across the country.

What we're witnessing is not just growth --**it 's revival. **

At Turning Point USA, we are dedicated and honored to continue strengthening the faith of Americans, young and old.

We are building a coalition of truth-preaching churches that stand firm against cultural compromise, defend biblical values, and strengthen families.

We are training pastors, uniting congregations, and, of course, reaching the next generation on campuses across the country with this same message.

You might feel disheartened by the evil in our culture and by the unthinkable assassination of Charlie.

**But America 's faithful are waking up. The youth are waking up. America is waking up. **

All across this nation, pastors are linking arms, young believers are finding their voice, and families are saying, _" We're not backing down." _

This is what Charlie prayed for.

I see this book as one of Charlie's most enduring gifts to the world, and I know you will too.

None of us knew how brief his time on earth would be. But the truths written in this book are timeless. They will outlive us all, and most importantly, **_so will the legacy of Charlie 's faith. _**

Charlie lived life at a relentless pace, but he also understood the sacred value of stillness. Through it all, his gaze was fixed on eternity with God.

Peter, I want to take stock of what we’re up against this year. We are in the middle of a full-fledged national redistricting crisis. It’s an emergency that’s been manufactured by an out-of-control administration. Donald Trump and his anti-democracy allies in states across the country are manipulating their congressional maps in an attempt to cling to power in the midterm elections. They want you to think they are unstoppable, but their desperation is obvious. **This will be far from easy, but it's a winnable fight.** We can even see cracks emerging in the facade. Just look at Indiana, where voters spoke out and inspired lawmakers of both parties to reject a new gerrymander — doing so in the face of threats of violence and reportedly even threats from the White House to withhold federal funding for the state. I wish that were the end of it. But we have reason to believe this redistricting crisis is about to get a whole lot worse. In Florida, Ron DeSantis has vowed to move forward with another extreme gerrymander attempt. At this very moment, several other states are also actively considering mid-decade redraws of their maps — some pointing to a forthcoming Supreme Court ruling on the Voting Rights Act as their anticipated justification. The task ahead of us is daunting. We must be prepared for all of it. There is no one coming to make the other side play fair — no cavalry coming to ensure that the will of the people will prevail on its own. I’ve said it before, and it bears repeating: **You and I, we are the cavalry our democracy depends on.** [**If you can, make a donation today to ensure that we can continue to fight back against power grabs across the country and uphold our democracy at this consequential moment in its history.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124440164/598616688/1128139581?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_WinnableFight_email_20260131-NDRC-Tier1-WinnableFight_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260131-NDRC-Tier1-WinnableFight_&utm_campaign=WinnableFight&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImNiOTI1YWVjLWI2ZmUtZjAxMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=zvNyGV0NhvCIEU2GtUefWyyeK-mGR5605sPaorSnOVw=) Together, we can prevail. body:
#
Peter —
I am reaching out myself because I need to ask a favor. We have a budget deadline tonight, and we are still short of where we need to be.
As it stands, if we don’t fill this hole, we’ll be forced to have a tough conversation tomorrow about where we have to cut back. It could derail us at the worst time.
We’ve seen that we are surging in the polls at just the right time. We’re on the air across the state and our 13,000 volunteers are organizing in every community in Texas and in multiple languages. We are meeting people wherever they are.
But this is a significant undertaking. It’s not cheap to organize everywhere and make sure voters — from the border to the panhandle — are invited into this people-powered movement to take back Texas from billionaires and their puppet politicians. Because it won’t happen unless all of us come together to play a role.
I’m grateful for this team. The outpouring of support means the world to me. I sincerely mean it, and I hope you know that I do not make these asks lightly.
We can’t falter now — not when we are in such a strong position and this close to our goal. So please:

Y’all, I get that I’m not a traditional candidate. But that’s exactly why I’m going to win.
**This race is about whether we keep chasing an idea of electability that hasn’t delivered — or whether we finally have the courage to try a different way. One rooted in faith, justice, turnout, and telling the truth about what Texans are facing right now.**

subject: Hey did this come through?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Cameron for Senate Inc
body:
| | | |
Hey Friend,
Really appreciate you taking the time to open this, I know you're busy.
This is Daniel Cameron and I want to talk with you for a second from one American to another.
I know you've been helping candidates and causes for some time because you love this country and know it's been in big trouble.
Sometimes it's hard to believe what's going on, let alone keep up with it all.
Who ever thought we'd actually have to fight over the idea of securing our border and deporting dangerous criminals? It's all so crazy.
I got into public service because I care about defending our Judeo-Christian values and our Constitution, and being a dad to two young boys with a third on the way, I'm reminded how important some of these foundational things really are.
I'm not sure how you feel, but ever since President Trump's unbelievable comeback victory in 2024, I've felt a wind at my back. I truly feel that God has given our nation a second chance, and I want to run as fast as possible to the front lines of this fight to help in any way I can.
That's why I'm running for Senate. We have a window of opportunity, and it's not going to be open forever. If we're going to take back ground from the Left and actually save this country, it will require principled fighters with a track record who are willing to take on the Democrats, the media, and even our own party from time to time.
[I believe I am the man for that moment, and your support before this month's deadline would be so helpful. It may still seem very early, but the primary is just over three months away. So even if it's just a few dollars, your help would mean a great to the whole team and me.](https://cameronsenate.acemlnc.com/lt.php?x=4lZy~GE5IITPEsGuzd5GUuhw23VUudL1k-U0jqXKVqbMDX.tyEy7x.Nz23.Rzk~w_x6tXXHJMnKa7q382NxGW.J)
The Democrats think they've got this year locked up. I'm sorry, but I'm not seeing it. Under President Trump's leadership, we're doing all the right things and we can't allow ourselves to fall victim to pessimism. We have to be realistic yes. But we have agency. We don't have to sit around and wait for things to happen. We have to go out and do the work and deliver a victory. With your help, I will do exactly that.
I have such high hopes for this country, and I hope you do as well.
Thanks for anything you can do, it's a real honor to have you on my side.
Sincerely, Daniel Cameron

body:
EMILYs List just endorsed my campaign.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Big news, Peter,
**EMILYs List has officially endorsed my campaign!**
Their support means so much to me, and I’m proud to have the backing of an organization that has spent decades uplifting pro-choice leaders who aren’t afraid to take on tough fights and lead with integrity.
At a moment when Texas families are suffering under the weight of rising costs and fending off relentless attacks on our personal freedoms, it’s clear that we can’t afford another four years of Greg Abbott. It’s time to turn the page — Texans are ready for a governor that puts people over profits, holds elected leadership accountable, and serves our communities with the same fighting spirit that runs through Texans every day.

> _“Gina Hinojosa is a proven fighter for Texans. Throughout her career, she has taken on corruption, stood up to corporate greed, and delivered — securing funding for public schools, expanding access to health care, and lowering costs for working families. While Gov. Greg Abbott puts billionaire donors first, Gina always puts Texans first. EMILYs List is proud to stand with Gina as she fights for Texas families.”
_
And that’s exactly what I’ll do, Peter. I’ll fight relentlessly for Texans every day, the same as I’ve done my entire career. I’m honored to stand alongside EMILYs List and our grassroots supporters across the state who believe Texas can, and must, do better.

Gina

body:
Reintroducing myself.
Hi Peter,
I’m Roy Cooper. _I'm running to be the next U.S. Senator from North Carolina, the most-likely Senate seat to flip. And together, we’re going to win._
You may know this about me already, but before I ask for your financial support ahead of my January fundraising deadline, I want to take a moment to reintroduce myself and remind you why I’m in this race — and why I’m counting on you to be in it with me.
**_[If you don’t need to read more, you can go ahead and split a donation between our campaign and Heartland Patriots now.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/100265?refcode=em20260131-10009&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10009%2E614464%2E_Ibuy1)_**

I’m a proud father and husband. I’m a lifelong North Carolinian. The Carolina Hurricanes’ #1 fan. And I was honored to serve North Carolina as Governor, Attorney General, and a legislator.
🩺 During my time in office, I fought hard to expand Medicaid. It wasn’t easy — it took nearly a decade of advocacy, negotiation, and perseverance — but we got it done. And it brought 700,000 North Carolinians access to the care they need.
♻️ I helped build North Carolina’s clean energy economy, which brought good jobs to our communities while helping protect our environment for future generations.
♀️ Over and over, I used every power at my disposal to try to defend reproductive health care access from the far-right’s cruel, dangerous, anti-freedom abortion bans.
Peter, this state is my home. I wanted to serve North Carolina and our communities from right here — I didn’t plan on trying to go to Washington. But when I look at what’s happening in this country today, I know I can’t leave things as they are for my children, or for yours.
I’m running for the U.S. Senate because I’m fed up with seeing extreme politicians strip away our rights, drive up the cost of living, tear apart our democracy and gut health care and SNAP benefits for folks in need. I’m ready for the fight, and I’m ready to deliver for the people. But I can’t get to Washington without your help. **[We have a $500,000 online fundraising goal to meet this month, and falling behind might give the GOP the momentum they need to surge ahead. Peter, We have all watched with horror as President Donald Trump’s masked agents terrorized Minnesota and led to the deaths of two American citizens. **Alex Pretti and Renee Good should be alive.** The responsibility for their deaths lies solely with the administration of Donald Trump, and his decision to sic armed, untrained federal agents into American cities and onto American citizens. Like many of you, we continue to watch these events with worry for our country’s future. But the way Americans have responded gives me great hope. Hoosiers of all political stripes do not want their daily lives upended by the presence of naked, armed agents with little to no training at their schools, grocery stores, and places of worship. **[Today, we’re asking you to sign our petition demanding accountability for ICE’s actions and constitutional violations in the wake of these killings. When I launched my 2022 campaign for State House in a district Trump won handily twice, almost no one thought I could win. It took sweat and determination and a lot of face-to-face conversations, but I ended up winning that race by – _get this_ – SIX votes. Seriously. Democracy Docket: With New Order, Trump Tries to Kill Off Vote By Mail [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=013126_1&amount=25]
We're going to keep hammering this home, Team, because the mainstream media continues to ignore this executive order and how it will change our elections forever.
President Donald Trump's massive anti-voting executive order has sent lawmakers, election officials, and voting rights advocates into a frenzy. One provision focuses on a goal that for years has been a borderline obsession for MAGA: Cracking down on voting by mail .
For background: After every election in which he's been a candidate or in power, Trump has raged over the use of mail-in ballots in general and ballot deadlines in particular . He's tried to claim fraud for every single ballot counted after Election Day.
So of course, this order directs Attorney General Pam Bondi to “ take all necessary action ” against any states that count absentee or mail-in ballots received after Election Day.
This order makes it clear that the MAGA crew will do anything they can to codify their power permanently and silence the will of the people by suppressing and eliminating the votes we cast.

We all know that mail-in voting laws are about ballot accessibility, making it easier for voters to participate in our elections . Elderly voters, the disabled, our military service members -- they all vote by mail.
Mail-in voting has happened dating back to the Civil War. It's always been safe and secure , mail-in voting fraud is supremely rare. States have spent millions of taxpayer dollars investigating voter fraud since 2020's "big lie" and found virtually nothing. It's been used widely in some states for decades and in most of the country since the pandemic.
Our partners at VoteAmerica said it best: “ There is no good-faith reason to limit vote-by-mail access, reject ballots without postmarks, or refuse to count ballots that arrive after Election Day. If the administration moves forward with these proposals, they will effectively disenfranchise older voters, rural voters, and military voters. ”
Opponents of voting rights have proven they'll go to any length necessary to stop people from voting and make sure that they stay in power. body:
Monday night marks Judge Chris Taylor’s first public fundraising deadline of the year.
# [](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/18?refcode=em20260131-1074&t=1&akid=1074%2E294397%2EoPL5D2)
[](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/31?c0=em_ms_jct_20260131_1_ak.kGEL6u&amount=10&refcode=em20260131-1074&t=3&akid=1074%2E294397%2EoPL5D2)
Hi there,
I’m reaching out today because Monday night marks Judge Chris Taylor’s first public fundraising deadline of the year.
With her general election just three months away, we can’t afford to leave anything to chance.
[**Before I say more, will you join me in supporting Judge Chris Taylor by chipping in $10 or any amount today?**](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/31?c0=em_ms_jct_20260131_1_ak.kGEL6u&amount=10&refcode=em20260131-1074&t=4&akid=1074%2E294397%2EoPL5D2)
You’ve seen how competitive these races are.
Last year, the Wisconsin Supreme Court majority was nearly flipped by right-wing special interests and billionaires like Elon Musk trying to buy a seat on the bench.
Now, they’re eyeing up Judge Chris Taylor’s race, and we’re expecting them to spend _big_ once again to try and install someone who will put their extreme agenda ahead of our rights.
That’s why I’m all in for Chris.
From her years as a public servant to her work on the bench, she’s spent her whole career standing up for people and protecting our freedoms. She’s fair. She’s tough. And she’s exactly the kind of justice we need on the Supreme Court.
**But this race won’t be won on values alone. It’s going to take a strong, people-powered movement to fight back — and that starts with showing strength before this deadline.**
[**Can you chip in $10 to help Judge Chris Taylor hit her $50,000 online goal before Monday night?**](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/31?c0=em_ms_jct_20260131_1_ak.kGEL6u&amount=10&refcode=em20260131-1074&t=5&akid=1074%2E294397%2EoPL5D2)

Thanks for being in this fight with us.
— Tammy

| | Peter,

I am a survivor of child trafficking--and today, I work to make sure other children never face what I did. My name is Theresa Flores. **I was fifteen years old.****An honor student.
****A daughter.
****A girl who trusted the wrong "friend. "**I was trafficked for two years.Most people imagine trafficking happens far away - in dark alleys or foreign countries. **To "other people."**But my nightmare happened in the suburbs of Detroit.I lived at home.
I went to high school.
**And no one noticed.** On the worst night of my life, I was taken to a dirty motel room and auctioned off to nearly two dozen men.**I remember the smell of the room.
****The fear in my chest.
****And the silence I was forced to keep.** I survived.But many do not.

That's why I partner with the **Sound of Freedom Foundation.** Through education and intervention, they equip frontline partners to do what most systems never taught--_help ordinary people to recognize trafficking before it 's too late._ Partners supported by **Sound of Freedom Foundation** train hotel employees--men and women working in places like the motel I was taken to -- to see what they were never taught to look for.**To notice what others miss.
****And to report it.** This is how **prevention becomes possible**. Because one informed employee and one brave phone call can save a life.**Here's the truth most people don 't know.**The majority of trafficking in America happens in hotels and motels.And it spikes around large sports events, conventions and concerts - anywhere demand increases. **There 's more you should know. **
---
* Human trafficking is the second-largest criminal enterprise in the world.
* **In the United States alone, 9 out of 10 missing children are trafficked.**
* If a child is not found within 48 hours, the risk of trafficking skyrockets.

name: Morgan Stahr, United for Democracy
subject: This Minnesota judge is holding ICE accountable
disclaimer_text: Paid for by United for Democracy
body:
A judge in Minnesota is standing up to ICE SIgn our petition to Congress urging them to do the same. | |
---
Peter, **A federal judge in Minnesota officially put ICE on notice this week, saying the court’s patience with them “is at an end.”** 1 On Monday, Chief Judge Patrick J. Schiltz was reviewing a case of a man named Juan, who had been snatched and removed to a detention facility in Texas—and was still waiting for a hearing over a week later. Chief Judge Schiltz had clearly had enough of ICE’s lawlessness. **In response, he ordered acting director of ICE Todd Lyons to appear in court or be held in contempt for violating countless court orders.** Schiltz said he understood this was an “extraordinary step” by the court, but that “the extent of ICE’s violation of court orders is likewise extraordinary, and lesser measures have been tried and failed.” **This is the energy we need from our court system right now—extraordinary measures for accountability and justice.** If the courts can stand up to ICE, then Congress can, too. The Senate is still debating the appropriations bills that fund the government, and Senate Democrats have said they will block funding bills that include money for the Department of Homeland Security, the agency that oversees ICE. Democrats must hold firm on this promise -- no money for ICE. [**The courts should be using every tool at their disposal to fight back against ICE’s violence and terror right now. Congress must join them in these efforts. Sign our petition now urging our representatives to stand up for justice and deny funding to ICE now!**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38jvf5GaclcQ7i_R9B-DMhJuIlivWC09O6g1TaXMbHFYp-cqhWOxu13nDY1n2nti1ohKf-GiKu-uoQwfXkKLNfifEsGA-Gep4JBV5s1rcZzsEZFGtpFVASMBIM3FvKxVbAVW3d-lYzU0lbC-8dMVCEC0n5053n6WAfECD9afqk2K4sFkfbsH49jALda9FsMWeEM_le7sO20OmezNVBMLcEHj0mTDnxxvUoDRnV1JMiJpFxw8jXCOjnvTY9xTXvr_VhhNBSTvMDN0Gn3ZTYTLb-r5eyTF2ao_YfPEiH3AvJ-4Q5kmMVFmfJdairUl_YcHn3WxtYJUC-4yJLwmm7Hv4Oismw7CLLpHYtK4u0iI5bvsXKJmfYbP8s4Y9Ju1yhgT6U/4nr/g8Xkt0xkSQ-TfNJw_OA8UQ/h0/h001.3bThOH2wrPnOndooYGvdtteQn0gcti729Sy3Pttvag8) [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38jvf5GaclcQ7i_R9B-DMhJuIlivWC09O6g1TaXMbHFYp-cqhWOxu13nDY1n2nti1ohKf-GiKu-uoQwfXkKLNfiq9PLpRyZv_8qnHsj1fSp1AC-d8PDNd-WKjpIHXJZ9Gss3ZkIvAb_qQGuKQRI4fOMhXW8QQiRJN9DLI91OIu-JiSvUcBtOgpRN86U9R5M36joBfa7ACPtrbKBWdUpMJpyJG5crHnKX64lGPOikRirGJFAwug9N6C5sepGFsKfFXZ8d99fB0ZkZItSKoAV7BZ3jqVQw2sTxSps0rDQhr66Q6ExKV_JRPaLrnNGGKoK2PgB7iSU3T9X0HBoLN2oJaWCWMDFfo0U4koyfgUivV5cW9b_2J3mP3V3yKoTI2Pp26k/4nr/g8Xkt0xkSQ-TfNJw_OA8UQ/h1/h001.-fW2b24qr2Y7H-1C11aVCEnMk8xAoHasCEA8e_9YMvs) Thank you for fighting to reform the Supreme Court, Morgan Stahr

Don’t let lies go unanswered

| |

Friend, Last night, Seth went on Sean Hannity, a show most Democrats avoid. Democrats cannot keep surrendering entire audiences to platforms built to defend Donald Trump and spread outright falsehoods about our values. Seth didn’t go on Hannity to change the host’s mind. That was never the point. He went on to confront lies head-on and speak directly to millions of Americans who rarely see Democrats push back in real time. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124450560/598645797/2090747700?refcode=260131_tm_hannity_icymi_img&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MGViMTcxMi1jM2ZlLWYwMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zAZpbJkwaYDzgabjYFuRlIF1cnyLJ3SgNd06MJZ2PEk=) On the show, Seth asked why Hannity **wouldn't criticize Trump just one time** ; Hannity wouldn't respond. When **Seth said that he doesn't think anyone should be executed for kicking a taillight** , Hannity didn't have a response. It was only when Seth stated the obvious — that anyone who believes in American values shouldn't have a problem with those who break the law being prosecuted — that he got Hannity to begrudgingly mutter the words _I agree_. If we want to hold this administration accountable, we need leaders willing to show up where the misinformation is loudest and stand up to it. Letting lies go unanswered only gives them more room to take hold. **[If you want to see more leadership like this, direct, unafraid, and focused on fighting for our values, help power Seth’s campaign by making a contribution today.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124450561/598645798/2090747700?refcode=260131_tm_hannity_icymi_l1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MGViMTcxMi1jM2ZlLWYwMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zAZpbJkwaYDzgabjYFuRlIF1cnyLJ3SgNd06MJZ2PEk=)** | [PITCH IN](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124450562/598645799/1375639745?refcode=260131_tm_hannity_icymi_b1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MGViMTcxMi1jM2ZlLWYwMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zAZpbJkwaYDzgabjYFuRlIF1cnyLJ3SgNd06MJZ2PEk=)

body:
Let's be honest for a second, Peter: politics feels exhausting right now.

Opening a political email during all this uncertainty can make you wonder: _Does any of this even move the needle anymore?_ You're not wrong to feel that way. A lot of people are worn down — and frankly, that's what this administration is counting on right now.

Under Donald Trump, we've watched abuse of power become routine. We've seen democratic norms shrugged off as if they're optional. Communities are being targeted by brutal ICE agents, and too many politicians are cheering it all on or staying silent and complacent.

It makes you want to tune out, and, at this point, _it's hard to blame anyone who does._ But, listen: **The GOP's chaos is intentional. It's dangerous to ignore the reality of what's going on in our country right now.**

Wesley is staying in this fight because of moments like this, not in spite of them. We deserve leaders with a backbone and a moral compass, and a government that works for the people it serves.

If we want checks on power, if we want dignity and decency back in government, if we want to flip the House and actually stop the worst abuses of power, then you need to stay engaged. All this can happen, but only if people like you decide not to give up.

| | Charlie would have wanted you to have this.

Before his September 10th assassination, Charlie had just put the finishing touches on a very important book. His final book.

The topic is one that Charlie found to be crucial for every human to understand and practice.

This isn’t a book about public policy or political discourse, nor is it simply about passing on values of patriotism to young Americans.

**Instead, this book is about something far deeper and more personal — the importance of honoring the Sabbath and resting in God’s grace.**

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children.

By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: _**“God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold.”**_

His book, _**Stop, in the Name of God**_ is the fruit of that conviction.
---
[](https://trk.americanmediawatchdog.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=t9qmmm&__onlt=h)
---
When you read it, you will hear Charlie’s voice inviting you to reclaim something our fast-paced culture has essentially erased: a time for rest, a time devoted to God, and time with family.

Charlie’s hope was for each of us to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive...

A sacred routine meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and renew our strength for the battles to which He calls us.

I believe you will find this book inspiring.

Charlie wanted everyone to have this book because its message meant so much in his own life.

**[To claim your copy of this life-changing book, simply make a generous gift in any amount to Turning Point USA today.](https://trk.americanmediawatchdog.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=t9qmmm&__onlt=h)**

---
In the months since Charlie’s assassination, there has been a massive surge of interest in Turning Point USA’s message among young Americans...

...and it’s not just the conservative message as a whole — _**it’s the message of FAITH!**_

In recent months, I have heard countless stories of people who have answered Charlie’s call to attend a Bible study, start a family, and pray to God.

Charlie devoted so much of his time urging people to build strong families, to go to church, and to stand up for America. _And it’s happening._

After years of witnessing declining church attendance, we are now seeing Americans filling the pews in huge numbers across the country.

What we’re witnessing is not just growth —**it’s revival.**

At Turning Point USA, we are dedicated and honored to continue strengthening the faith of Americans, young and old.

We are building a coalition of truth-preaching churches that stand firm against cultural compromise, defend biblical values, and strengthen families.

We are training pastors, uniting congregations, and, of course, reaching the next generation on campuses across the country with this same message.

You might feel disheartened by the evil in our culture and by the unthinkable assassination of Charlie.

**But America’s faithful are waking up. The youth are waking up. America is waking up.**

All across this nation, pastors are linking arms, young believers are finding their voice, and families are saying, _“We’re not backing down.”_

This is what Charlie prayed for.

I see this book as one of Charlie’s most enduring gifts to the world, and I know you will too.

None of us knew how brief his time on earth would be. But the truths written in this book are timeless. They will outlive us all, and most importantly, **_so will the legacy of Charlie’s faith._**

Charlie lived life at a relentless pace, but he also understood the sacred value of stillness. Through it all, his gaze was fixed on eternity with God.

**[To claim your copy of Charlie’s final book, simply make a gift, in any amount, to support Turning Point USA today.](https://trk.americanmediawatchdog.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=t9qmmm&__onlt=h)**

---
I’ll personally ensure your copy is sent to you as soon as possible.

Thank you in advance for carrying on Charlie’s mission and supporting his legacy.
---
**For Charlie,**

**Justin Streiff**
Chief Operating Officer
Turning Point USA

**My whole life led me to this moment. **
**I spent decades as a sideline reporter for professional football and basketball. I covered more Minnesota games than I can count. And I raised two children with my husband outside Minneapolis. I love Minnesota. **
**However, what 's happening here hits a little too close to home. **
**1. I watched as Tim Walz sent my tax dollars to fraudulent daycares. 2. I watched as career politicians handed out billions to illegal immigrants while our veterans slept on the streets. 3. | [](https://substack.com/redirect/5ea8900a-1091-4943-b4db-59018e0dff3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Idaho just introduced a bill to "protect kids from social media"...
Finally, right? Something that actually targets Instagram and TikTok instead of making device manufacturers responsible for Meta's mess. This is a far better idea than targeting device manufacturers like [App Store Accountability Acts](https://substack.com/redirect/c75719fa-20cb-489c-9117-14e238c152f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) do.
[H0542](https://substack.com/redirect/5a6ccf33-f7fa-418d-bc53-cef34fc68673?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) would force platforms to get parental consent before kids under 17 can create accounts. It would strip out the addictive features like infinite scrolling and autoplay for children and make platforms verify ages and give parents monitoring tools.
Sounds like exactly what we need.
Except when you read the fine print, something feels off.
Yes, it makes social media companies responsible for age verification. And it makes them remove addictive features from kids' accounts (that's the right target, we don't want device manufacturers to play police).
_Except why do we need the government to do what parents can already do?_
Because, while well-intentioned, this bill requires covered platforms to get "verifiable parental consent" before creating accounts for kids 16 and under. Platforms have to remove infinite scrolling, autoplay, push notifications for children's accounts.
You know what else removes those features? Not giving your kid an Instagram account.
Instead, this creates a whole infrastructure for parental oversight through the platform. But parents already control whether their kid has a phone or apps.
You don't need Meta to build you a "monitoring dashboard."
You just... take the phone.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4cfd811e-f233-4bc2-9903-ee50ac55fa4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
With this bill, companies like Meta have to estimate ages after 25 hours of use with 80% confidence. Then again at 50 hours with 90% confidence (keeps updating estimates every 100 hours).
**But Meta already knows roughly how old their users are.**
They collect birthdates. Their algorithms can infer age from behavior. They target ads to "13-year-old girls interested in fitness" with surgical precision. They're not struggling to figure out who's a kid.
The problem isn't that social media companies can't identify children. It's that their entire business model depends on serving addictive algorithmic content to those children regardless of what harm it causes.
_**If you 're an engaged parent who monitors your kid's online activity this bill gives you exactly zero new power you don't already have. **_
You can say no to Instagram already. But if you're a checked-out parent who gave unrestricted device access? You'll click "approve" on the verifiable parental consent without reading it just like every Terms of Service you click through.
Your teenager will access social media through friends' phones, web browsers, or the thousand workarounds kids have perfected.
Because the bill only covers accounts, not access. So the only thing this really accomplishes is forcing platforms to build expensive compliance systems while parents maintain the same level of actual control they always had.
Section 48-2106 says waivers of rights under this chapter are "void ab initio" and courts can't enforce them.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9803f31d-3a74-4c50-af66-0db499a8e6ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Now there are two ways to read this:**
**(1)** The harsh interpretation: the government is deciding that even if you as a parent review the terms, understand the risks, and consent to your 15-year-old having an Instagram account, that decision is automatically invalid as "contrary to public policy." Your informed parental choices about your own child are void as a matter of law. The government overrides parental authority while claiming to protect it.
**(2)** The more charitable interpretation: the bill prevents platforms from pressuring parents into signing away the law's protections through Terms of Service fine print. Meta couldn't get you to contractually agree to let them skip removing infinite scrolling or waive your right to sue if they violate requirements. That would actually be protective.
_But here 's where it gets murky. _
The section says waivers of "any prohibition, requirement, or right to remedies" are void. So what counts as a waiver? Is your informed decision to let your kid have an Instagram account despite the law's restrictions a "waiver" of protections? Or is it just parenting?
The bill requires verifiable parental consent to create accounts. So it recognizes parental authority to say yes. But then this section says parents can't waive the specific protections the law mandates.
Maybe the intended reading is: _you can consent to your kid having an account, but you can 't consent to Meta violating the specific requirements like removing addictive features._
That would be less about replacing parental authority and more about preventing platforms from exploiting parents with misleading contracts.
**Either way, the ambiguity is a problem.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5d0a60f8-82a6-45d9-9a69-812fb49a8a33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The bill also exempts accounts that have existed "continuously for at least seven years."
So if your kid opened an Instagram account at age 10 (lying about their age, which happens constantly), by the time they're 17 the platform has no obligation to verify anything. That exemption exists because forcing social media companies to age-verify millions of long-standing accounts would be impossibly expensive.
But it also means the kids who've been on these platforms longest get zero protections.
The bill also requires platforms to notify account holders before termination and give them 30 days to dispute age classification. This is a legal requirement, yes. But during the 30-day window the kid gets to keep using the platform exactly as before.
So we're creating this massive regulatory apparatus that platforms can avoid by simply making age verification annoying enough that kids learn to game the system.
Private right of action with $10,000 statutory damages for reckless violations sounds tough, right? But Meta spent $24 million on lobbying in 2024 alone. More than Lockheed Martin. So they can afford armies of lawyers who will argue about what constitutes "reasonable means" for age estimation. Every case will get fought and every loss will get appealed.
**Meanwhile, your 13-year-old is still scrolling through eating disorder content at 2am because you gave them a smartphone with unrestricted access and kept it in their bedroom.**
You want to protect your kid from social media?
Don't give them a smartphone until they're older. Give them a flip phone if they need to stay in touch. Say no to social media and actually enforce it. Check their devices regularly. Keep phones out of bedrooms at night.
Those are parenting decisions that work immediately. You don't need legislative infrastructure or enforcement mechanisms. Age estimation algorithms? Also not needed.
_Idaho House Bill 542 treats the symptom instead of the cause._
And the cause? It's parents handing their 12-year-olds unrestricted access to devices that Jonathan Haidt calls "the world's most sophisticated drug delivery device" and then acting surprised when those kids develop anxiety and depression.
You made deliberate choices with predictable consequences.
_**It 's like giving your kid a handful of razor blades to play with and getting mad at the store who sold them to you when your kid gets hurt. **_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/15763cc1-1205-45e3-bee7-c06261dff5cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This bill targets the right entities. That's progress. Removing infinite scrolling and push notifications from verified children's accounts could reduce some addictive features. And if platforms can't show targeted ads to kids, that removes one harm vector. Maybe that helps marginally.
_**But it 's still asking the government to regulate your kid's social media consumption because you won't.**_
And Meta will comply with the minimum requirements while finding new ways to maximize engagement and profit.
If this moves forward, platforms will figure out compliance. Lawyers will spend years in court arguing over definitions. Meanwhile regulations will get expanded to catch what the previous version missed, then expanded again when platforms find new workarounds.
But your kid will still be on Instagram unless you actually say no.
That's the part no legislation can fix.
* * *
## **TLDR Idaho H542:**
1. **Gives you zero new power** \- you already control whether your kid has a phone and social media
2. **Has easy workarounds** \- kids access through friends' phones, web browsers, and all the other methods bill doesn't cover
3. **Has a 7-year exemption backfire** \- because a kid who lied about their age at 10 gets zero protections by age 17 (the kids on platforms longest)
4. **Has a 30-day loophole** \- legally the platforms must notify before termination, which means the kid gets to keep using it during the "dispute period"
5. **Is compliance theater** \- platforms will build expensive systems while algorithms keep serving addictive content that falls just outside statutory definitions
6. **Solves the wrong problem** \- platforms monitor because parents won't
7. **Lets social media companies win anyway** \- they'll spend millions on lawyers and compliance, not fixing the harm their algorithms cause
8. **Treats the symptom not the cause** \- because it regulates features while ignoring that parents handed kids unrestricted access to "the world's most sophisticated drug delivery device"

Because, while well-intentioned, this bill requires covered platforms to get "verifiable parental consent" before creating accounts for kids 16 and under. Platforms have to remove infinite scrolling, autoplay, push notifications for children's accounts. You know what else removes those features? Not giving your kid an Instagram account. Instead, this creates a whole infrastructure for parental oversight through the platform. But parents already control whether their kid has a phone or apps. You don't need Meta to build you a "monitoring dashboard." You just... take the phone. | | ---|---|--- With this bill, companies like Meta have to estimate ages after 25 hours of use with 80% confidence. Then again at 50 hours with 90% confidence (keeps updating estimates every 100 hours). But Meta already knows roughly how old their users are. They collect birthdates. Their algorithms can infer age from behavior. They target ads to "13-year-old girls interested in fitness" with surgical precision. They're not struggling to figure out who's a kid. The problem isn't that social media companies can't identify children. It's that their entire business model depends on serving addictive algorithmic content to those children regardless of what harm it causes. If you 're an engaged parent who monitors your kid's online activity this bill gives you exactly zero new power you don't already have. You can say no to Instagram already. But if you're a checked-out parent who gave unrestricted device access? You'll click "approve" on the verifiable parental consent without reading it just like every Terms of Service you click through. Your teenager will access social media through friends' phones, web browsers, or the thousand workarounds kids have perfected. Because the bill only covers accounts, not access. So the only thing this really accomplishes is forcing platforms to build expensive compliance systems while parents maintain the same level of actual control they always had. Section 48-2106 says waivers of rights under this chapter are "void ab initio" and courts can't enforce them. | | ---|---|--- Now there are two ways to read this: (1) The harsh interpretation: the government is deciding that even if you as a parent review the terms, understand the risks, and consent to your 15-year-old having an Instagram account, that decision is automatically invalid as "contrary to public policy." Your informed parental choices about your own child are void as a matter of law. The government overrides parental authority while claiming to protect it. (2) The more charitable interpretation: the bill prevents platforms from pressuring parents into signing away the law's protections through Terms of Service fine print. Meta couldn't get you to contractually agree to let them skip removing infinite scrolling or waive your right to sue if they violate requirements. That would actually be protective. But here 's where it gets murky. The section says waivers of "any prohibition, requirement, or right to remedies" are void. So what counts as a waiver? Is your informed decision to let your kid have an Instagram account despite the law's restrictions a "waiver" of protections? Or is it just parenting? The bill requires verifiable parental consent to create accounts. So it recognizes parental authority to say yes. But then this section says parents can't waive the specific protections the law mandates. Maybe the intended reading is: you can consent to your kid having an account, but you can 't consent to Meta violating the specific requirements like removing addictive features. That would be less about replacing parental authority and more about preventing platforms from exploiting parents with misleading contracts. Either way, the ambiguity is a problem. | | ---|---|--- The bill also exempts accounts that have existed "continuously for at least seven years." So if your kid opened an Instagram account at age 10 (lying about their age, which happens constantly), by the time they're 17 the platform has no obligation to verify anything. That exemption exists because forcing social media companies to age-verify millions of long-standing accounts would be impossibly expensive. But it also means the kids who've been on these platforms longest get zero protections. The bill also requires platforms to notify account holders before termination and give them 30 days to dispute age classification. This is a legal requirement, yes. But during the 30-day window the kid gets to keep using the platform exactly as before. So we're creating this massive regulatory apparatus that platforms can avoid by simply making age verification annoying enough that kids learn to game the system. Private right of action with $10,000 statutory damages for reckless violations sounds tough, right? But Meta spent $24 million on lobbying in 2024 alone. More than Lockheed Martin. So they can afford armies of lawyers who will argue about what constitutes "reasonable means" for age estimation. Every case will get fought and every loss will get appealed. Meanwhile, your 13-year-old is still scrolling through eating disorder content at 2am because you gave them a smartphone with unrestricted access and kept it in their bedroom. You want to protect your kid from social media? Don't give them a smartphone until they're older. Give them a flip phone if they need to stay in touch. Say no to social media and actually enforce it. Check their devices regularly. Keep phones out of bedrooms at night. Those are parenting decisions that work immediately. You don't need legislative infrastructure or enforcement mechanisms. Age estimation algorithms? Also not needed. Idaho House Bill 542 treats the symptom instead of the cause. And the cause? It's parents handing their 12-year-olds unrestricted access to devices that Jonathan Haidt calls "the world's most sophisticated drug delivery device" and then acting surprised when those kids develop anxiety and depression. You made deliberate choices with predictable consequences. It 's like giving your kid a handful of razor blades to play with and getting mad at the store who sold them to you when your kid gets hurt. | | ---|---|--- This bill targets the right entities. That's progress. Removing infinite scrolling and push notifications from verified children's accounts could reduce some addictive features. And if platforms can't show targeted ads to kids, that removes one harm vector. Maybe that helps marginally. But it 's still asking the government to regulate your kid's social media consumption because you won't. And Meta will comply with the minimum requirements while finding new ways to maximize engagement and profit. If this moves forward, platforms will figure out compliance. Lawyers will spend years in court arguing over definitions. Meanwhile regulations will get expanded to catch what the previous version missed, then expanded again when platforms find new workarounds. But your kid will still be on Instagram unless you actually say no. That's the part no legislation can fix. TLDR Idaho H542: 1. Gives you zero new power \- you already control whether your kid has a phone and social media 2. Has easy workarounds \- kids access through friends' phones, web browsers, and all the other methods bill doesn't cover 3. Has a 7-year exemption backfire \- because a kid who lied about their age at 10 gets zero protections by age 17 (the kids on platforms longest) 4. Has a 30-day loophole \- legally the platforms must notify before termination, which means the kid gets to keep using it during the "dispute period" 5. Is compliance theater \- platforms will build expensive systems while algorithms keep serving addictive content that falls just outside statutory definitions 6. Solves the wrong problem \- platforms monitor because parents won't 7. Lets social media companies win anyway \- they'll spend millions on lawyers and compliance, not fixing the harm their algorithms cause 8. Treats the symptom not the cause** \- because it regulates features while ignoring that parents handed kids unrestricted access to "the world's most sophisticated drug delivery device" | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Brian Lenney ? ?

* * *
In this week's _Weekly Wrapup_ , **David Shuster** delivered a sharp, fast-moving breakdown of a news cycle defined by authoritarian abuse of power, institutional rot, and moments of grim absurdity that now feel routine in Trump's America.
The week opened with chaos at the Department of Justice, which abruptly released--and then just as quickly removed--more than three million pages of Jeffrey Epstein files. According to Shuster, the documents included deeply disturbing allegations involving **Donald Trump** , including claims of sexual assault of underage girls and grotesque descriptions of events allegedly held at Mar-a-Lago. The DOJ's explanation, delivered by Trump's former personal attorney now serving as Deputy Attorney General, rang hollow when the files vanished minutes after posting, replaced by a "page not found" notice. The timing and reversal raised immediate red flags about transparency, obstruction, and selective enforcement.
That same day brought another vanishing act--this time at movie theaters. A heavily promoted documentary centered on Melania Trump quietly began disappearing from cinemas after dismal ticket sales. Shuster highlighted the financial absurdity: Amazon reportedly paid $40 million for the film and spent $35 million more promoting it, despite projections of only $1-2 million in opening-week revenue. In Hollywood terms, that math only makes sense if the movie was never really about box office success at all.
* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.wiZkI7jEJcLtmAmbD__tZA9p2oWOfOBPS3Ic2MvC3sU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=186422886)
* * *
The week's most chilling development came in Georgia, where FBI agents raided a Fulton County election center and seized records connected to the 2020 election--six years after Trump famously pressured state officials to "find" votes. Shuster underscored how unprecedented it was for the Director of National Intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard, to personally participate in the execution of a search warrant, calling it a fundamental breach of law-enforcement norms.
In Minnesota, fallout continued from the killing of 37-year-old Alex Pretti by ICE agents. After officials falsely portrayed Pretti as violent, both Kristi Noem and ICE commander Greg Bovino were sidelined and replaced by border czar Tom Homan. Shuster noted the grim irony that authorities were now touting "progress" because ICE had gone an entire week without killing anyone.
The episode closed with two tonal pivots: a tribute to a utility lineman risking his life to restore power during brutal winter storms, and an AI-generated satire mocking the same ICE commander recently removed from his post. Shuster's sign-off captured the moment perfectly: keep laughing, keep smiling--and stay strong.
* * *
## 🔑 Top Takeaways
1. The DOJ's Epstein file release-and-removal raises serious questions about obstruction and political protection.
2. The Melania documentary's finances suggest influence-peddling, not filmmaking.
3. Federal law enforcement is increasingly being weaponized against elections and dissent.
4. ICE accountability remains shockingly minimal--even after lethal force.
5. Gallows humor is becoming a survival mechanism in a collapsing civic culture.

In this week's Weekly Wrapup , David Shuster delivered a sharp, fast-moving breakdown of a news cycle defined by authoritarian abuse of power, institutional rot, and moments of grim absurdity that now feel routine in Trump's America. The week opened with chaos at the Department of Justice, which abruptly released--and then just as quickly removed--more than three million pages of Jeffrey Epstein files. According to Shuster, the documents included deeply disturbing allegations involving Donald Trump , including claims of sexual assault of underage girls and grotesque descriptions of events allegedly held at Mar-a-Lago. The DOJ's explanation, delivered by Trump's former personal attorney now serving as Deputy Attorney General, rang hollow when the files vanished minutes after posting, replaced by a "page not found" notice. The timing and reversal raised immediate red flags about transparency, obstruction, and selective enforcement. That same day brought another vanishing act--this time at movie theaters. A heavily promoted documentary centered on Melania Trump quietly began disappearing from cinemas after dismal ticket sales. Shuster highlighted the financial absurdity: Amazon reportedly paid $40 million for the film and spent $35 million more promoting it, despite projections of only $1-2 million in opening-week revenue. In Hollywood terms, that math only makes sense if the movie was never really about box office success at all. The week's most chilling development came in Georgia, where FBI agents raided a Fulton County election center and seized records connected to the 2020 election--six years after Trump famously pressured state officials to "find" votes. Shuster underscored how unprecedented it was for the Director of National Intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard, to personally participate in the execution of a search warrant, calling it a fundamental breach of law-enforcement norms. In Minnesota, fallout continued from the killing of 37-year-old Alex Pretti by ICE agents. After officials falsely portrayed Pretti as violent, both Kristi Noem and ICE commander Greg Bovino were sidelined and replaced by border czar Tom Homan. Shuster noted the grim irony that authorities were now touting "progress" because ICE had gone an entire week without killing anyone. The episode closed with two tonal pivots: a tribute to a utility lineman risking his life to restore power during brutal winter storms, and an AI-generated satire mocking the same ICE commander recently removed from his post. Shuster's sign-off captured the moment perfectly: keep laughing, keep smiling--and stay strong. 🔑 Top Takeaways 1. The DOJ's Epstein file release-and-removal raises serious questions about obstruction and political protection. 2. The Melania documentary's finances suggest influence-peddling, not filmmaking. 3. Federal law enforcement is increasingly being weaponized against elections and dissent. 4. ICE accountability remains shockingly minimal--even after lethal force. 5. Gallows humor is becoming a survival mechanism in a collapsing civic culture. | | ---|---|--- READ OUR OPEN LETTER TO SUBSTACK | | and | | ---|---|--- | Jan 30 | MORE FROM BLUE AMP MEDIA * You're currently a free subscriber to . | | Charlie would have wanted you to have this.

Before his September 10th assassination, Charlie had just put the finishing touches on a very important book. His final book.

The topic is one that Charlie found to be crucial for every human to understand and practice.

This isn't a book about public policy or political discourse, nor is it simply about passing on values of patriotism to young Americans.

**Instead, this book is about something far deeper and more personal -- the importance of honoring the Sabbath and resting in God's grace. **

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children.

By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: _**" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." **_

His book, _**Stop, in the Name of God**_ is the fruit of that conviction.

Charlie's hope was for each of us to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive...

A sacred routine meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and renew our strength for the battles to which He calls us.

I believe you will find this book inspiring.

Charlie wanted everyone to have this book because its message meant so much in his own life.

In the months since Charlie's assassination, there has been a massive surge of interest in Turning Point USA's message among young Americans...

...and it's not just the conservative message as a whole -- _**it 's the message of FAITH! **_

In recent months, I have heard countless stories of people who have answered Charlie's call to attend a Bible study, start a family, and pray to God.

Charlie devoted so much of his time urging people to build strong families, to go to church, and to stand up for America. _And it 's happening. _

After years of witnessing declining church attendance, we are now seeing Americans filling the pews in huge numbers across the country.

What we're witnessing is not just growth --**it 's revival. **

At Turning Point USA, we are dedicated and honored to continue strengthening the faith of Americans, young and old.

We are building a coalition of truth-preaching churches that stand firm against cultural compromise, defend biblical values, and strengthen families.

We are training pastors, uniting congregations, and, of course, reaching the next generation on campuses across the country with this same message.

You might feel disheartened by the evil in our culture and by the unthinkable assassination of Charlie.

**But America 's faithful are waking up. The youth are waking up. America is waking up. **

All across this nation, pastors are linking arms, young believers are finding their voice, and families are saying, _" We're not backing down." _

This is what Charlie prayed for.

I see this book as one of Charlie's most enduring gifts to the world, and I know you will too.

None of us knew how brief his time on earth would be. But the truths written in this book are timeless. They will outlive us all, and most importantly, **_so will the legacy of Charlie 's faith. _**

Charlie lived life at a relentless pace, but he also understood the sacred value of stillness. Through it all, his gaze was fixed on eternity with God.

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children. By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: " God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." Charlie's hope was for each of us to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive... A sacred routine meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and renew our strength for the battles to which He calls us. I believe you will find this book inspiring. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
